source_caption_text:
23 years ago today, Ye released “Through the Wire,” and the rest is history 🐐🔥🔥

The track became unforgettable because Ye recorded it while his jaw was wired shut after a serious car accident. He built the song around a sped-up sample of Chaka Khan’s “Through the Fire,” turning the injury into part of the record itself. The studio footage of him shaping it with a full choir makes the creative process feel like watching a classic take form in real time. 🎨

“Through the Wire” went on to become the lead single from The College Dropout and earned a Grammy nomination for Best Rap Solo Performance. More than two decades later, the story behind the song is still just as striking as the record.
